artists.biography:
Tori Amos (born Myra Ellen Amos; August 22, 1963) is an American pianist, singer-songwriter and composer. She is a classically trained musician and possesses a mezzo-soprano vocal range. Amos originally served as the lead singer of 1980s synthpop group Y Kant Tori Read, and as a solo artist was at the forefront of a number of female singer-songwriters in the early 1990s. She was also noteworthy early in her solo career as one of the few alternative rock performers to use a piano as her primary instrument. Some of her charting singles include "Crucify", "Silent All These Years", "God", "Cornflake Girl", "Caught a Lite Sneeze", "Professional Widow", "Spark", "1000 Oceans", and "A Sorta Fairytale", her most commercially successful single in the U.S. to date.
 
As of 2005, Amos had sold 12 million albums worldwide. She has been nominated for several awards, including 8 Grammy Award nominations. Amos was also named one of People Magazine's 50 Most Beautiful People in 1996.

perplexity.description:
Little Earthquakes – The B-Sides" is a compilation album featuring the B-sides from the singles released from Tori Amos's debut solo album Little Earthquakes (1992). The original Little Earthquakes album marked Amos's transition from her earlier synth-pop band to a more intimate, piano-driven rock and pop style, blending confessional songwriting with complex emotional themes. This B-sides collection complements the original album by showcasing additional material recorded during the same era, highlighting Amos's depth as a songwriter and performer beyond the main album tracks.

Musically, the B-sides maintain the rock and pop sensibilities of Little Earthquakes, characterized by Amos's distinctive piano work and expressive vocals. The compilation offers fans a deeper look into the creative output surrounding the debut, including rarities and alternate versions that reinforce the emotional intensity and lyrical introspection that defined the original album. Although the B-sides album itself was originally released in a limited edition and did not have the commercial impact of the debut, it is valued for its insight into Amos's early artistic development and has been reissued on vinyl by Rhino Records and Atlantic, underscoring its enduring appeal.

The original Little Earthquakes album, released in 1992, received critical acclaim for its raw, personal songwriting and helped establish Amos as a significant voice in 1990s alternative rock and pop. While the B-sides collection did not chart independently, it is regarded as an important companion piece that enriches the understanding of Amos's breakthrough period and her evolution as a solo artist.
